results.question: Why are Chinese AI models primarily open source?
results.answer: Publishing weights gets a model adopted quickly, because inference providers and developers can run it the day it ships instead of waiting on the lab's own API. US chip export controls also play a part, as CSIS has argued, since third-party hosts take on serving costs a Chinese lab would otherwise carry, although open releases make the models harder to monetize. Strictly speaking, most of these are open weight models rather than fully open source, since the training data stays private, and some flagships stay closed, including Baidu's ERNIE 5.0 and ByteDance's Dola Seed 2.0 Pro.

items.question: Why are Chinese AI models primarily open source?
items.answer: Publishing weights gets a model adopted quickly, because inference providers and developers can run it the day it ships instead of waiting on the lab's own API. US chip export controls also play a part, as CSIS has argued, since third-party hosts take on serving costs a Chinese lab would otherwise carry, although open releases make the models harder to monetize. Strictly speaking, most of these are open weight models rather than fully open source, since the training data stays private, and some flagships stay closed, including Baidu's ERNIE 5.0 and ByteDance's Dola Seed 2.0 Pro.

items.answer: An independent, MIT-licensed community project published November 1–2, 2026 — not affiliated with Liquid AI — that wires four of Liquid's LFM3 models into a supervised local agent stack: a d1-2B router, an LFM3-1.7B actor, LFM3-VL-2B for vision and LFM3-Audio-2B for voice, all pinned to CPU llama.cpp servers on 127.0.0.1. Its own benchmark run caught its router silently faking itself — the failure mode the harness exists to catch.
